newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Enerco encouraged by oil/gas exploration.
newsitem.headline: Enerco encouraged by oil/gas exploration.

text.p: WELLINGTON, April 16 - There are encouraging signs of an oil or gas field with up to 50 million barrels of hydrocarbons on the East Coast, joint venture explorers gas retailer Enerco and Westech Energy, the Dominion newspaper said on Wednesday.
United States Westech Energy managing director Ed Davis, in New Zealand this week, said the companies were pleased with progress after initial exploration in the under-explored "wildcat" area.
"It has the potential to be a large find," Davis said.

The partners plan to drill three wells next year and if they find oil, production could start almost immediately. If there was a gas find it would take longer to set up supply gas lines to Hawke's Bay, presently supplied from Taranaki.
Enerco chief executive Kevin Johnson said a big gas find would mean customers in Hawke's Bay should get a lower cost of supply than the cost of the present supply from Taranaki.
The partners believed the coast could become another Taranaki, with its various gas and oil fields.
Five wells have been drilled on the East Coast before and all have failed to make a commercial discovery, but technology has improved since those wells were drilled.
Davis believed the earlier explorers probably did not drill enough holes.
"We have just finished the initial seismic reconnaissance survey, about 275 kilometres, and we are presently getting early impressions -- initially we are quite encouraged," he said.
"There are strong indications that there is a very good source rock." There were good signs for "favourable structural styles".
Westech and Enerco plan to carry out more detailed infill seismic testing later in the year as a follow-up from the results. The infill work would give them the appropriate spots to drill.
The prospective area is the central third of the onshore concessions held by the partners, around Wairoa.
The partners are targeting sandstone at between 2000 and 3000 metres and are looking for both gas and oil.
The area is generally under-explored, with only one offshore well drilled.
Enerco is mainly interested in gas for supply to East Coast customers, but any oil find would be a bonus, Johnson said.
Bringing gas from Taranaki was expensive and with deregulation, transmission charges would depend on the length of the pipeline.
"The further you are away from Taranaki, the more it is going to cost," he said.
That cost had been a significant spur in the hunt for gas on the East Coast.

Pipeline operator Natural Gas Corporation sells gas to Enerco in Hawke's Bay in a bundled form, with costs for energy and transmission grouped together. With deregulation there would be variable transmission cost.
-- Wellington Newsroom (64-4-4734746)
